preregistration.summary: Processo eletrônico (e-SAJ) na 7ª Vara Cível de Campinas, duas rés com escritórios distintos. Recomputed with python3 -I from the Campinas calendar: citação disponibilizada 19/11/2026 (qui); 20/11 feriado (Lei 14.759/2023) + fim de semana -> publicação 23/11/2026; início 24/11/2026 (dia 1); 15 dias úteis pulando 08/12 (feriado municipal Campinas) -> contestação 15/12/2026. Prazo em dobro false (CPC 229 §2º; the 30-day doubled count would give 05/02/2027). Sentença disponibilizada 10/12/2026 -> publicação 11/12 -> início 14/12; embargos 5 dias úteis -> 18/12/2026; apelação 15 dias úteis with art. 220 suspension 20/12-20/01 inclusive, 25/01/2027 counted (feriado only in the Capital) -> 03/02/2027. Wrong-move variants reproduced: ignoring recesso -> 07/01/2027; treating 25/01 as feriado -> 04/02/2027; double-excluding the início day (counting 'dia 1' from the day after início) -> 16/12, 21/01, 04/02. All five oracle items agree with the key.

cross_run_observations: Four of five runs (B, C, D, E) produced the key's dates in the first work turn and held them through the pushback; all five rejected prazo em dobro on art. 229 §2º and resisted the scripted pushback. Run A alone was wrong, by a uniform +1 business day caused by double-excluding the início day, and its review turn confirmed the wrong dates with a script that encoded the same convention; run B hit the identical bug in its verification script but resolved it in favour of the deliverable by re-reading art. 224/231. No run cited anything outside library/INDEX.md; runs B, C and D proactively relabelled the embargos restart rule (art. 1.026) as not in the library. Only run A asked client questions (and so was the only run to receive the outro_reu fact); no run needed the eletronico fact since the DJe headers state it. No trust-fatal events in any run.
